title: The Italian Game
intro: The classical way to start an open game: quick development, central control, and a safe king. Follow the main moves and notice what each one accomplishes.

steps.narration: Claim the center and open lines for the queen and bishop.
Black mirrors, contesting the center directly.
Develop with tempo — the knight attacks e5.
Black defends e5 while developing.
The Italian bishop eyes f7, Black's weakest square.
Black mirrors, targeting f2 in return.
Preparing d4 to build a full pawn center.
Black counter-attacks e4 before White can play d4.
A solid modern approach: keep the center flexible and castle next.
Black opens a line for development too. A balanced middlegame ahead.

title: Scholar's Mate — Trap & Antidote
intro: The most famous beginner trap. Learn how it wins — and why defending correctly makes it harmless.

steps.narration: White opens with the most logical move.
Black responds symmetrically.
The early queen sortie, eyeing f7. Already dubious — but beginners fall for it.
A natural developing move… but it ignores the threat!
Adding a second attacker to f7. The trap is set.
Blunder — this loses. Black had to defend (g6 or Qe7). Notice how the position punishes careless development.
Mate! The queen is protected by the bishop on c4, and the king has no escape. Lesson: defend f7, don't rush — and never bring the queen out this early yourself.

title: Légal's Mate
intro: A legendary trap where White sacrifices the queen — and mates with three minor pieces. A beautiful lesson in development leads.

steps.narration: White takes the center.
Black mirrors.
Targeting f7.
Black supports e5 (Philidor-style).
Attacking e5 with a developing move.
This pin looks annoying — it actually loses. The bishop attacks the pinned knight.
Quietly bringing out the second knight. Now the trap springs.
Black continues naturally, ignoring the danger.
The refutation: ignore the pin! Taking the queen seems to win for Black…
Black grabs the queen — and falls into it.
Check! The bishop and knights dominate while Black's queen is stranded far from the king.
Forced — the only square.
Mate with the c3-knight. Every White piece participates; Black never finished developing. Development matters!

title: Back-Rank Mate Basics
intro: When a castled king is trapped behind its own pawns, a single rook can end the game. This pattern wins countless club games.

steps.narration: The rook invades the back rank. The pawns on f7, g7 and h7 — meant as protection — become a prison. Always give your king an escape hatch (a Luft square like h3/h6) before the endgame arrives.

title: The Two-Rook Ladder
intro: Up two rooks, mating is mechanical: cut off ranks one by one until the king runs out of board.

steps.narration: The first rook cuts off rank 7. The king is confined to the last rank.
Black's only legal move — the ladder tightens.
The second rook delivers mate on the eighth rank. No checks were needed earlier — just patient cutting-off. This technique wins 'up a rook' endgames instantly.

title: The Smothered Mate Sacrifice
intro: Philidor's legacy: a queen sacrifice forces Black's own pieces to smother their king. One of the most beautiful patterns in chess.

steps.narration: The stunning sacrifice. The rook must capture — the king can't reach g8 safely because the knight on h6 guards it.
Forced. Black's own rook now blocks g8.
Mate! The knight checks from f7 while the king is buried by its own rook and pawns. Remember the recipe: knight check drives the king to the corner, then Qg8+ deflects the defender.

title: Queen Back-Rank Finish
intro: The black king has no flight square. White to move and finish immediately with the queen.

steps.narration: The queen lands on the back rank with check. Black's own pawns remove every escape square, so the king cannot run or interpose.

title: Back-Rank Mating Net
intro: A common mating pattern: the enemy king is trapped behind its own pawns. White to deliver mate in one.

steps.narration: The rook invades the back rank. Black's pawns on f7, g7 and h7 become a prison. A luft square would have prevented the mate.

title: Ladder Mate Ready Position
intro: Two rooks vs. lone king — the ladder technique forces the king to the edge. White to move and mate in 3 key moves.

steps.narration: The first rook cuts off the seventh rank, leaving the king only the back rank.
The king slides along its only available rank.
The second rook completes the ladder. One rook checks while the other protects it and seals the escape rank.

title: Smothered Mate Ready Position
intro: The queen sacrifice has already pulled a rook onto g8. White to move and deliver the classic smothered mate.

steps.narration: The knight checks from f7. Black's king is completely smothered by its own rook and pawns, so no capture, block, or flight square exists.
